content: {"answer_sections": [{"text": "Astypalaia served as a hideout for corsairs in the 17th century, offering safe anchorages and provisions like bread and wine.", "claim_ids": ["c-3b7330380fb024c7a959"]}, {"text": "In 1602, Spanish pirate Alonso de Contreras sought refuge on Phournoi after operations in Serifos, Astypalaia, Amorgos, and Patmos.", "claim_ids": ["c-e527d741eac628ba80a9"]}, {"text": "The Black Sea port of Azov was acquired by Russia in 1696, contributing to its naval policy under Peter I.", "claim_ids": ["c-53f369010e4ba9743338"]}, {"text": "The Ottoman Empire and its Barbary corsairs were identified as a common enemy of Malta and Russia.", "claim_ids": ["c-f88054ba713451967caf"]}], "unknowns": ["The exact locations of other anchorages and hideouts in the Eastern Mediterranean during 1600–1700 remain unspecified in the sources.", "The relationship between the Ottoman Empire and Barbary corsairs as described is not elaborated in the provided sources."], "limitations": ["Sources are secondary and require further critical examination.", "Some claims lack detailed geographic or temporal specifics beyond what is explicitly stated."]}
